name: Butter Chicken Pasta

ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz dry short pasta (penne, rigatoni or rotini)

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredients are used by a step; no step uses an unbought item. Reserved pasta water is water, not a purchased line.
Per-serving protein locks at 40.2 g, clearing the >=40 floor by only 0.2 g. Flag for repair pass: verify the built spec does not drop under 40 after the cost/macro pass.

Prose carries no dollar figure except the {{cost_ps}} token and the standard $1/month membership line. No cost_lines were provided in dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce or lasts-N-batches claims.
Portioning uses the weigh-the-pot method across 14 containers per house convention.
Cuisine labeled Indian Fusion because the dish sets butter chicken sauce over pasta rather than rice.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a dish that does something sneaky and wonderful at the same time. It takes butter chicken, the creamy tomato curry that gets people to fall in love with Indian food, and it pours the whole thing over pasta instead of rice. Purists might raise an eyebrow. Your wallet and your weeknight will not. You get the warm garam masala, cumin and coriander perfume, a tomato sauce mellowed with almond butter and half and half, and tender bites of chicken breast, all clinging to short pasta that holds sauce the way rice never quite does.

Let me be straight with you about why this earns a spot in the rotation. It hits ${{cost_ps}} a serving, it lands 40.2 grams of protein and 630 calories per container, and it scales to fourteen dinners from one pot. That is comfort food math that actually adds up.
prose.shop_smart:
• Grab any sturdy short pasta you like. Penne, rigatoni or rotini all work because their ridges and tubes trap the sauce. Buy the whole 2 lb 5 oz you need in one or two boxes rather than scrounging odds and ends, so every serving cooks to the same al dente.
  • Boneless skinless chicken breast is the backbone here, and 3 1/2 pounds is the size that family packs are built for. Buy the big pack, not the little tray, and cut it into bite-sized pieces yourself.
  • The spice shelf is where this recipe pays you back. Garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder and turmeric are all measured in teaspoons, so one small jar of each carries you through this batch with plenty left for the next round of curry night.
  • Passata, sold as tomato sauce or strained tomatoes, is the smooth base. Buy it plain with no added seasoning so your own spices lead. You need 7 cups, so check the carton or jar size and get enough.
  • Almond butter and half and half are the two that make the sauce silky. A scant half cup of almond butter and 3 1/2 cups of half and half is all it takes, so buy the smallest sizes that cover it.
  • Fresh ginger and a bunch of cilantro do the finishing work. A thumb of ginger covers the 3 1/2 tablespoons, and one bunch of cilantro gives you the 1 1/2 cups of leaves with stems to spare.
prose.make_it:
Start the pasta first so it is ready when the sauce is. Boil your short pasta to al dente per the package, and before you drain it, dip out a cup or two of that starchy pasta water and set it aside. That water is your thickening insurance later, so do not skip it.

In a large pan over medium heat, warm the olive oil and butter together. Add the chicken and let it cook until it is golden on all sides. Do not crowd it, and do not stir it to death. You want color, not steam.

Now stir in the diced onion, garlic and ginger, and cook for two to three minutes until they soften and smell like the good part of a curry house. Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric and red pepper flakes, and cook for just one minute, stirring constantly so the spices bloom in the fat and do not scorch.

Stir in the tomato paste and the tomato sauce and let it come together. If it looks too thick, loosen it with a splash of that reserved pasta water. Stir in the almond butter until it melts in, then pour in the half and half. Bring it to a boil, drop the heat, and simmer four to five minutes until the sauce thickens and turns that glossy tomato-cream color.

Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss until every piece is coated. Stir in the chopped cilantro, season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste, and it is done.
prose.portion_html:
Here is the honest way to portion fourteen even servings, and it is not by eyeballing. Weigh the empty pot before you cook, or set the loaded pot on the scale and subtract in your head. Either way, once the pasta is tossed and coated, take the total weight of the food, divide by fourteen, and that number is your target for each container. Scoop, weigh, adjust, move on. It takes an extra two minutes and it is the difference between fourteen real dinners and eleven big ones with three sad scrapings at the end.

These containers hold up well through the week. The sauce keeps the pasta from drying out, and a splash of water before you reheat brings the whole thing right back to glossy.
prose.cost_closing_html: Fourteen dinners of butter chicken pasta at ${{cost_ps}} a serving is the kind of number that makes takeout feel like a tax. You are getting restaurant flavor, real protein at 40.2 grams a container, and a week of lunches or dinners handled, all from one pot and a few pantry spices you will use again and again.
prose.upsell_html: If a batch like this saves you even one delivery order a week, our whole membership costs about a dollar a month, and every recipe here is built the same honest way: real macros, real prices, real portions you can weigh. Cook once, eat well all week, and let the math work for you instead of against you.

head.description: Butter Chicken Pasta meal prep for 14 servings. Creamy tomato curry sauce with garam masala and tender chicken breast over short pasta, 630 calories and 40.2g protein per serving.

steps: Cook the short pasta to al dente per the package directions. Reserve 1 to 2 cups of pasta water, then drain.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook until golden on all sides.
Stir in the onion, garlic and ginger and cook 2 to 3 minutes until softened.
Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric and red pepper flakes. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the tomato paste and tomato sauce and stir to combine. Loosen with a little reserved pasta water if it looks too thick.
Stir in the almond butter, then add the half and half. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until thickened.
Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss to coat well in the sauce.
Stir in the chopped cilantro, season with salt and black pepper to taste, and serve.
